results.question: Why does channel stock tend to rise right after each quarter-end?
results.answer_text: Channel stock (channel_stock_units) climbs in the last two weeks of each fiscal quarter and then unwinds: e.g. it rose from ~1.91M units in the week of 2026-02-23 to ~2.50M by 2026-03-30, and from ~1.84M to ~2.25M into the March 2025 quarter-end. The pre-registered stuffing detector flags this as quarter-end channel stuffing — distributors ordering well above their trailing-90-day rate in the scheme window (last 15 days), with 280 distributor-category flags in FY26Q4 and 276 in FY25Q4 (stuffing_flags metric). So the post-quarter-end stock build-up is driven by scheme-window order loading ahead of quarter close, not by a change in sell-out.
sql:
SELECT
  subq_5.metric_time__week AS metric_time__week
  , SUM(subq_5.__channel_stock_units) AS channel_stock_units
FROM (
  SELECT
    channel_stock_units AS __channel_stock_units
    , week_start__week
    , metric_time__week
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS week_start__week
      , DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS metric_time__week
      , days_of_stock is not null AS inventory_week__has_days_of_stock
      , stock_units AS channel_stock_units
    FROM "marts"."mart_channel_inventory_weekly" channel_inventory_src_10000
    WHERE DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) BETWEEN '2026-01-26' AND '2026-04-05'
  ) subq_4
  WHERE inventory_week__has_days_of_stock
) subq_5
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    metric_time__week
    , MAX(week_start__week) AS week_start__week__complete
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS week_start__week
      , DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS metric_time__week

results.question: Warranty claim costs were higher in FY26 than in FY25. What drove the increase?
results.answer_text: Warranty claim cost rose from ₹23.53M in FY25 to ₹29.48M in FY26 (warranty_claim_cost), and the increase is almost entirely base cracks: base-crack cost went from ₹19.34M to ₹24.88M (+₹5.54M), while all other failure modes together added only about ₹0.4M. The lot_scan anomaly detector flags resin lot RL-DGP-L2-250310 (DGP plant, line 2) as a base-crack outlier — 291 claims vs ~76 expected (effect size 3.84, p≈9e-79) — and that single lot accounts for ₹2.30M of FY26 base-crack cost, the largest lot-level driver. So the FY26 increase is driven by a base-crack quality problem concentrated in DGP line-2 resin lots, led by lot RL-DGP-L2-250310.

results.question: Sell-out in Assam jumped in Q1 FY27 (April to June 2026) compared with Q1 FY26. Which distributor drove most of that growth, and what was behind it?
results.answer_text: New Biswas Traders (D0118) drove most of Assam's Q1 FY27 sell-out growth: its secondary units rose from 56,862 in Q1 FY26 to 87,669 in Q1 FY27, a gain of about 30,807 units — the largest single-distributor increase in the state (per the secondary_units metric). The growth was broad-based across the quarter (30,798 / 28,029 / 28,842 units in April, May, June 2026) and concentrated in fittings (58,650 vs 35,084 a year earlier, led by CPVC Elbow 20 mm at 16,850 vs 8,700 and CPVC Tee 20 mm at 12,500 vs 8,100), with pipes also up (26,832 vs 20,083). It was genuine sell-through rather than channel loading: primary (sell-in) units tracked sell-out closely (99,068 vs 87,669), and the stuffing detector raised no flag for D0118 in Q1 FY27.
